dataset.name: Candidate-committee linkage file
dataset.description: FEC assertions linking candidate IDs to committee IDs, with distinct candidate election year, FEC election period, committee type, designation, and linkage identity.

acquisition.pagination: None. Each requested two-year period is one complete ZIP snapshot.

partitions.name: two_year_period
partitions.source: Requested bulk URL path; cycle_suffix is the period's final two digits.
partitions.purpose: Acquisition and replay boundary. It must agree with FEC_ELECTION_YR before publication.

acquisition.retry_policy: Bound retries for transport failures; follow redirects; publish only after validating the HTTP result, ZIP integrity, exact member name, archive digest, row width, and record count.

physical_schema.line_ending: LF with a required final LF in the verified 2020, 2022, 2024, and 2026 artifacts
physical_schema.empty_record_policy: An empty physical line becomes an explicit record-boundary issue; it is never silently skipped.
physical_schema.null_policy: Preserve every empty source field as the empty string; required identity and year fields failing their schema become issues rather than invented values.

identity.occurrence_locator: archive SHA-256 + exact member name + one-based physical line number
identity.record_version: occurrence locator + SHA-256 of the exact source line
identity.duplicate_policy: Preserve every physical occurrence. A repeated LINKAGE_ID with conflicting content blocks relationship publication; equivalent repeats remain separately auditable occurrences.

time_fields.meaning: Requested bulk archive period and acquisition boundary.
Candidate election year attached to this relationship; it can precede the FEC election period.
FEC two-year period in which the linkage assertion is published.

code_fields.meaning: Raw committee type code attached to the linkage.
Raw committee designation code attached to the linkage.

rules: Keep source_partition.two_year_period, FEC_ELECTION_YR, and CAND_ELECTION_YR separate.
A linkage is a source-backed relationship assertion, not proof that every committee transaction is candidate-controlled.
Preserve designation and committee type as filed before interpreting authorized, principal, or joint-fundraising roles.
Do not discard prior candidate-election-year linkages from a later FEC period.
Do not infer candidate-to-committee relationships from names when a linkage record is absent.

revisions.publisher_model: The FEC replaces the two-year linkage archive as registrations change; LINKAGE_ID identifies a published linkage but does not version changing snapshots.
revisions.effective_projection: Blocked while draft. Preserve every archive snapshot and linkage occurrence; publish a relationship only from an accepted snapshot with no identity conflict.

checks.rule: The archive digest, requested period, exact ccl.txt member, retrieval time, and response metadata are present.
Every physical line has exactly 7 fields; short rows are not padded and extra fields are not truncated.
Every source byte decodes under the accepted encoding; invalid bytes are retained as failed raw evidence, never silently dropped.
Every non-empty physical line becomes one record occurrence or one explicit issue.
Conflicting records for one LINKAGE_ID remain separate and block relationship publication.
Member name, field order, or field count changes require contract review.

scenarios: distinct candidate and FEC election years

use.retention: Retain the exact archive, HTTP metadata, archive digest, member inventory, record occurrences, and issues indefinitely; derived graph relationships are rebuildable.
use.disclaimer: This file reports FEC candidate-committee linkage assertions for a captured snapshot. Relationship designation must remain visible and does not alone establish control of each receipt or disbursement.
